body.p: AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS The following listing of claims replaces all previous listings and versions of claims in this application.

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A method of adjusting analyte sensor data, comprising:
storing, by processing circuitry, at least one parameter including a slope associated with a sensitivity of an analyte sensor;
collecting, by the processing circuity, sensor data from the analyte sensor when the analyte sensor is at least partially inserted into interstitial fluid of a user, the sensor data including data indicative of a level of an analyte in the interstitial fluid;
obtaining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf start time from an electronic memory communicatively coupled with the processing circuitry;
determining, by the processing circuitry, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor based on the shelf start time;
obtaining, by the processing circuity, a shelf duration of the analyte sensor;
adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration, the adjusting comprising adjusting the slope associated with the sensitivity of the analyte sensor;
determining, by the processing circuitry, the level of the analyte of the user from the sensor data using the adjusted slope; and
outputting the determined level of the analyte to a display.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 3, wherein the shelf duration is representative of a period of time after the analyte sensor was manufactured and before the analyte sensor was inserted into the interstitial fluid of the user human body.
5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 3, wherein the shelf duration includes the entire time the analyte sensor was in a packaged state prior to insertion into the interstitial fluid of the user human body.
6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 5, wherein a wait period is implemented such that the shelf duration is representative of a time period less than the entire time the analyte sensor was in a packaged state prior to insertion into the interstitial fluid of the user.
7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 3, wherein the determined level of the analyte adjusted sensor data is different from the collected sensor data.
8. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the at least one parameter one or more parameters further comprises an intercept, and wherein adjusting, by processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration further comprises adjusting the intercept.
9. (Cancelled)
10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 3, further comprising collecting temperature data representative of a plurality of temperatures to which the analyte sensor was subjected during the shelf duration.
11. (Original) The method of claim 10, further comprising adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration and the plurality of temperatures.
12. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 1, further comprising determining a wear duration with processing circuitry, and adjusting, by the processing circuitry, processing of the sensor data to compensate for the wear duration.
13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein the wear duration is representative of a period of time during which the analyte sensor is at least partially inserted into the interstitial fluid of the user human body.
14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein the wear duration begins upon insertion of the analyte sensor into the interstitial fluid of the user human body.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 12, wherein a sensor control device comprises the analyte sensor and sensor electronics, and wherein the shelf duration ends wear duration begins upon activation of the sensor control device.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 claim 3, wherein adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data to compensate for the shelf duration comprises:
adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data with a continuous function comprising an adjustment parameter and a value representative of time.
24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment parameter corresponds to a code selected from one of a plurality of codes, the method further comprising:
decoding, with processing circuitry, the code to determine the adjustment parameter.
25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment parameter corresponds to a code selected from one of a plurality of codes, the method further comprising:
communicating the code from a sensor control device to a reader device;
decoding, with processing circuitry of the reader device, the code to determine the adjustment parameter; and
adjusting, with processing circuitry of the reader device, the sensor data with the continuous function comprising the adjustment parameter and the value representative of time.
26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the value representative of time is representative of [[a]] the shelf duration.
27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the value representative of time is representative of [[a]] the shelf duration less a wait period.
28. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the adjustment factor is stored in the electronic memory in an unencoded form, the method further comprising:
adjusting, with processing circuitry, the sensor data without decoding the adjustment factor.
